fixes.explanation: A road sounds calm, but that's not what she sings. She says he is “…leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.” Nobody leaps over a hill on the way to the mailbox. That's a whole different kind of walk.

Mourning isn't the word he picks, friend. He says, “For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.” Then he adds, “the season of singing has come…” Winter's behind them, and singing is the season he names.
True! The voice says, “…let me see your face, let me hear your voice…” He asks for both, her face and her voice. He adds, “for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.”

Close, but the text gives a different reason. The call is to catch “…the little foxes that ruin the vineyards…” and then comes “…for our vineyards are in bloom.” The vineyards are in bloom, and that's the reason given for catching the foxes.

Right, it's false. The text says, “Catch for us the foxes—the little foxes that ruin the vineyards—for our vineyards are in bloom.” The reason it gives is that the vineyards are in bloom, not that they're already ruined.
Not this time, friend. She says, “On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.” She looked and didn't find him. The song takes a turn here.
Right, it's false. She says, “I sought him, but did not find him.” She's on her bed at night, looking, and she doesn't find him. I think that's a long, quiet kind of night.
She says, “I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love.” She gets up and goes to look. The search moves out into the streets and squares.
She says, “I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city…” They were out on their rounds, and she ran into them. Watchmen, out in the city at night, and she meets them.
A flock came up earlier: “he pastures his flock among the lilies.” But out in the city at night, she says, “I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city…” Different scene entirely.
She asks, “Have you seen the one I love?” It's a simple question. She's out in the city at night, and the watchmen are who she asks.
Not warned, friend. She asks, “Have you seen the one I love?” Nobody's handing out warnings in this question, it's a search party of one. She just wants to know if the watchmen have spotted him.
True! She says, “I had just passed them when I found the one I love.” She asked the watchmen, moved on, and found him. All that searching and there he is.

She says, “I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.” She holds on until she's brought him there. That's some determination.

No king's chambers in this verse. She says, “I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house…” Her destination is her mother's house, “to the chamber of the one who conceived me.”
